draft.title: Government initiatives
card: An initiative is a planned action taken to improve something. Governments use initiatives to improve the wellbeing of the people they serve.
Governments fund hospitals, clinics and public schools. Healthy, educated people can work, earn and take part in community life.
Governments pay money to people who cannot earn enough, such as the unemployed, people with a disability and people who are retired. This helps them afford food, housing and other basics.
Governments build the systems a community relies on, such as water supply, sewage, roads and electricity. Clean water lowers the spread of disease, and roads link people to jobs, schools and clinics.
draft.remember: Governments improve wellbeing through services, payments and infrastructure.

a.q: Which government initiative is an example of building infrastructure?
opts: Laying pipes to bring clean water to a town
Paying an allowance to people who are unemployed
Opening a free vaccination clinic in a suburb
Hiring more teachers for a public primary school
a.why: Pipes for a water supply are a system a community relies on, so they are infrastructure. A payment is welfare, a clinic is health care and teachers provide schooling.
a.clue: Look for something physical that is built and used by a whole community.

b.q: A state government sealed the only road linking a remote town to its nearest hospital and high school. How does this initiative most directly improve wellbeing?
opts: It helps people reach health care and schooling
It gives residents a regular payment for living costs
It removes the need for a local clinic or school
It brings clean drinking water into every home
b.why: A road is infrastructure, and it links people to services such as health care and schooling. It is not a welfare payment, and it does not supply water. A road helps people reach services but does not replace them.
b.clue: Think about what the road connects the town to.

a.best: Laying pipes to bring clean water to a town

b.best: It helps people reach health care and schooling
